blocking.issue: The "both streams past the cap" regression can only ever exercise the stdout cap; the stderr cap branch is never reached by any committed test
blocking.evidence: MINI_BIG_MAIN writes stdout first and blocks: `sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"O" * 1572864)` (test_files.py:373) is a blocking 1.5 MiB write into a 64 KiB pipe, so the child cannot proceed to `sys.stderr.buffer.write(b"E" * 1572864)` (test_files.py:375) until the parent has drained it. The parent stops draining first: in support.py:143-155 buffers[0] reaches BOUND_OUTPUT_BYTES after 16 x 64 KiB reads, the 17th read gives room==0 and `len(piece) > max(room, 0)` raises ValueError, then _kill_owned_group SIGKILLs the child (support.py:148). The child is therefore killed ~1.06 MiB into its stdout write, having written zero bytes to stderr. The test's only assertion is `pytest.raises(ValueError, match="bound")` (test_files.py:431), which the stdout path alone satisfies, and it never asserts which stream the message names even though support.py:147,155 embeds it. Concretely: mutate support.py:132 to `index = 0` (never select the stderr buffer) or skip `os.set_blocking` for stderr only, and the suite stays green at 47 passed.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: The assignment brief line 94 requires the durable regressions to "Include both streams past the cap"; only one stream is covered, so the stderr half of required finding #2 (bound applied while reading) has no non-vacuous regression. The report compounds this by citing test_invoke_output_past_cap_is_typed_failure as the evidence for finding 2 in .pipeline/out/task-0-helper-repair.json:13 without noting the stdout-only reach.
blocking.fix: Add a stderr-only miniature target (write 1.5 MiB to stderr, nothing to stdout, then attempt the export) and a second case asserting `pytest.raises(ValueError, match="stderr")`; tighten the existing stdout case to `match="stdout"` so each stream's cap is independently pinned. Parametrizing one test over the stream name is sufficient; no production change is needed.

blocking.issue: _read_export_file keeps a plain blocking open() for absolute export names, bypassing the shared no-follow/non-blocking bounded reader that required finding #2 mandated
blocking.evidence: `if candidate.is_absolute(): with open(candidate, "rb") as handle: raw = handle.read(BOUND_OUTPUT_BYTES + 1)` is the only path in Task0's owned test/production code that opens a filesystem path outside the safe primitives; every sibling path uses F.read_regular (support.py:82, support.py:532), which deliberately supplies O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and an fstat S_ISREG check (src/ptest/files.py:135-163) precisely so "a FIFO can never wedge the caller". Consequences of the exception: (a) ordinary open() on a FIFO blocks in open(2) forever, and this call happens at support.py:518 AFTER _drain_bounded has already returned, i.e. outside every deadline the explicit keyword watchdog is supposed to guarantee — invoke hangs with no timeout at all; (b) open() follows symlinks, so an absolute export name that is a link reads the target, contradicting the path-ownership guarantee the relative branch enforces; (c) the frozen grammar declares `--result-json REL_FILE` (design line 58, restated line 82: "project-relative, validated non-symlink paths"), so the helper accepts and reads back a path shape the real CLI must reject. The branch is also dead today: no committed test passes an absolute --result-json (the generated name at support.py:486 is relative, and both override tests use "sub/result.json", test_files.py:465,553), so it is untested code carrying the only unbounded-time operation in invoke.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Required finding #2 (brief lines 85-86) says the export read-back must "use the shared bounded reader"; one branch does not, and it reintroduces exactly the unbounded-wait class the repair was ordered to remove, in a helper whose frozen contract is an explicit bounded watchdog.
blocking.fix: Delete the absolute branch: route every export name through `F.read_regular(Path(root), name, BOUND_OUTPUT_BYTES + 1)` and return None (or raise a typed fixture failure) for an absolute name, matching the frozen `--result-json REL_FILE` grammar. This removes three lines and the dead code path at once; no new test target is needed beyond an assertion that an absolute override yields result=None rather than an open().

notes: REFUTED (root hypothesis 3, main claim): the post-exit grace break does not silently truncate the child's own output. support.py:109 breaks only after _EXIT_DRAIN_GRACE_S=1.0s past exit, and a child that has exited cannot have more than the 64 KiB pipe buffer outstanding, which the 64 KiB reads at support.py:134 drain in one or two 50 ms iterations. The 1.05s duration of test_invoke_returns_when_child_exits_despite_retained_pipe in root-helper-scoped.log:14 matches the grace exactly, and the grace is what makes that required case (child exits while an owned grandchild retains the pipe) terminate at all. Bytes not captured after the break belong to the retained-pipe grandchild, not to the measured child.

REFUTED (root hypothesis 3, cleanup scope): cleanup is owned-only. invoke launches with start_new_session=True (support.py:503) and _kill_owned_group targets os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL) (support.py:68), never the caller's group or pid 0. test_invoke_watchdog_bounded_with_retained_pipe launches its `sleep 60` sentinel WITHOUT start_new_session (test_files.py:437), i.e. in pytest's own process group, and asserts it survives (test_files.py:447); root's durations show that test at 2.01s against timeout=2.0, so the watchdog is genuinely bounded. No orphan is left either: support.py:176 kills the owned group even on the success path, reaping the 30s grandchild of MINI_EXIT_RETAIN_MAIN.

RESIDUAL from hypothesis 3 (not required): _kill_owned_group is called at support.py:176 after proc.poll()/proc.wait() has already reaped the leader, so the pid is free for reuse at that moment. If the group is empty the killpg is a harmless ESRCH, and PID reuse needs a full pid_max wraparound, so this is theoretical — but it is the one place the helper could signal a process it does not own. Cheap hardening if ever revisited: capture the pgid before the final wait and skip the kill when poll() showed no surviving group members.

RESIDUAL from hypothesis 3 (not required): the descriptor-error paths collapse into apparent success. `except (OSError, ValueError): break` on select (support.py:129-130) and `live[index] = False` on a failing os.read (support.py:137-138) both fall through to the normal return at support.py:181, so a mid-run descriptor failure would return a normal Completed with silently truncated stdout/stderr rather than a typed failure — inconsistent with the deliberate typed ValueError chosen for the cap. I could not construct a reachable trigger: the only closer of these streams is the helper itself, and PEP 475 retries EINTR, so I am not reporting it as a defect. Worth a typed error instead of `break` if this code is ever touched again.

CONFIRMED but not required (root hypothesis 2): _WRAPPER_VALUE_OPTS (support.py:39) knows 2 of the ~11 options the frozen grammar puts in the wrapper prefix (design lines 56-58 also list --changed/--base/--full/--workers/--queue-timeout/--no-setup/--fresh/--local/--shadow). _prefix_result_json returns None at the first of those (support.py:44), so `case.invoke(d, r, '--shadow', '--result-json', 'out.json', timeout=...)` still generates its own export and ships a duplicate: [--fixture-domain D, --result-json GEN, --shadow, --result-json out.json]. The helper then reads GEN, which the child never wrote, and returns result=None — or the child rejects the duplicate with a usage exit. I tried to find a real consumer and could not: `--result-json` appears nowhere in the plan's example calls, and I traced all three documented consumers through the new code and they are correct (plan:344 `--` tail, plan:352 `--workers 2 -k --full`, plan:368 `--shadow`, each keeping the generated export inside the prefix). The report already discloses the boundary in not_verified. Smallest contract-safe resolution if a consumer ever needs it: extend the table with the frozen grammar's value-taking set (--fixture-domain/--base/--workers/--queue-timeout/--result-json) plus its flag set (--changed/--full/--no-setup/--fresh/--local/--shadow) and keep the same stop-at-unknown/`--` loop — a literal transcription of design lines 56-58, not a second parser and not permissive argparse.
